criteria_quotes: Single Level Fusion With or Without Decompression — Surgical Indications: When ALL of the following are present: Lumbar back pain, neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain without sensory or motor deficit that impairs daily activities for at least 6 months; Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months; ... Imaging studies corresponding to the clinical findings; At least ONE of the following clinical conditions: Spondylolisthesis ... Evidence of segmental instability ...

NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment. Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute 'inability to complete' treatment.

[Conservative treatment must include] at least two (2) of the following: Analgesics, steroids, and/or NSAIDs; Structured program of physical therapy; Structured home exercise program prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider or physician; Epidural steroid injections and/or selective nerve root block.

Operative treatment is indicated when the natural history of surgically treated lesions is better than the natural history for non-operatively treated lesions. All operative interventions must be based on a positive correlation with clinical findings, the natural history of the disease, the clinical course, and diagnostic tests or imaging results.

# Findings

I was not able to find an **Iowa Total Care/Ambetter Health‑branded copy** of a lumbar fusion medical policy on iowatotalcare.com or ambetterhealth.com. However, I was able to establish, from Iowa Total Care's/Ambetter Health of Iowa's own provider-facing pre‑authorization pages, that **prior authorization for spine surgery (including lumbar fusion) is delegated to Evolent Specialty Services, Inc. (formerly National Imaging Associates/NIA)**, a musculoskeletal‑surgery utilization‑management vendor used across Centene Corporation's affiliated health plans (Iowa Total Care/Ambetter Health is a Centene company). The Iowa Total Care clinical‑policy page also states that "Iowa Total Care may from time to time delegate utilization management of specific services; in such circumstances, the delegated vendor's guidelines may also be used to support medical necessity."

Evolent's governing criteria document for this CPT code is the **"Evolent Clinical Guideline for Lumbar Spine Surgery"** (internally numbered NIA_CG_304 in older editions and Evolent_CG_1766 in current editions), part of Evolent's annual "Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines" compendium. This guideline explicitly lists CPT 22612 under "Lumbar Fusion – Single Level," confirming it is the applicable criteria set for this procedure code. I verified this exact text via copies of the guideline posted by a sister Centene plan (Louisiana Healthcare Connections, filed with the Louisiana Dept. of Health) and via Evolent's public guideline repository (radmd.com), which is the same vendor/document family Iowa Total Care uses. I could not locate an Iowa Total Care–specific hosted PDF of this particular surgical guideline (only PT/OT and imaging guidelines are posted with an "Iowa Total Care" cover page on radmd.com), so I cannot certify that the exact copy applied to this member is identical, though the criteria have been substantively stable across the 2023–2026 editions I reviewed.

# Findings

I was not able to find an **Iowa Total Care/Ambetter Health‑branded copy** of a lumbar fusion medical policy on iowatotalcare.com or ambetterhealth.com. However, I was able to establish, from Iowa Total Care's/Ambetter Health of Iowa's own provider-facing pre‑authorization pages, that **prior authorization for spine surgery (including lumbar fusion) is delegated to Evolent Specialty Services, Inc. (formerly National Imaging Associates/NIA)**, a musculoskeletal‑surgery utilization‑management vendor used across Centene Corporation's affiliated health plans (Iowa Total Care/Ambetter Health is a Centene company). The Iowa Total Care clinical‑policy page also states that "Iowa Total Care may from time to time delegate utilization management of specific services; in such circumstances, the delegated vendor's guidelines may also be used to support medical necessity."

This guideline explicitly lists CPT 22612 under "Lumbar Fusion – Single Level," confirming it is the applicable criteria set for this procedure code. I verified this exact text via copies of the guideline posted by a sister Centene plan (Louisiana Healthcare Connections, filed with the Louisiana Dept. of Health) and via Evolent's public guideline repository (radmd.com), which is the same vendor/document family Iowa Total Care uses. I could not locate an Iowa Total Care–specific hosted PDF of this particular surgical guideline (only PT/OT and imaging guidelines are posted with an "Iowa Total Care" cover page on radmd.com), so I cannot certify that the exact copy applied to this member is identical, though the criteria have been substantively stable across the 2023–2026 editions I reviewed.
